subtopic: Alternative Mutual Funds vs. Hedge Funds
source_evidence: These protections include limits on illiquid investments, restrictions on borrowings and debt, and the requirement to allow investors to sell their shares at any time. Hedge funds are not required to follow these regulations, and therefore may pursue non-traditional strategies and investments without the same regulatory safeguards.
answer: Alternative mutual funds and hedge funds can use similar investments or strategies, but they are not the same type of fund. Alternative mutual funds are regulated as mutual funds, with safeguards that include limits on illiquid investments and borrowing, and investors must be allowed to sell their shares at any time. Hedge funds are not required to follow those same regulations, so they may operate without those safeguards.
